sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Monroe Township, Middlesex County?
sections.html:
Monroe Township in Middlesex County, the ZIP 08831 township around Jamesburg, is a market defined by age-restricted communities and long Turnpike commutes. It is a different place from Monroe Township in Gloucester County, with its own offices, fee chapter and tax appeal calendar.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 49,830 residents, up 2.4 percent since the April 2020 base. In the 2020 to 2024 survey 39.6 percent of residents were 65 or older and 91.1 percent of homes were owner occupied, the highest owner rate among the four towns in this group of pages. The median owner value is $540,900 and median household income is $107,892. Mean travel to work is 40.3 minutes, and 26.6 percent of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: What is Monroe Township's layout, and why do age-restricted communities matter?
sections.html:
Monroe was founded in April 1838, and at 42.19 square miles it is the largest municipality in Middlesex County by total area. It completely surrounds the borough of Jamesburg, one of 21 pairs of "doughnut" towns in New Jersey. Neighbors include Cranbury, East Brunswick, Helmetta, Old Bridge, South Brunswick and Spotswood in Middlesex County, East Windsor in Mercer County, and Manalapan and Millstone in Monmouth County.

The township turned suburban between 1960 and 1968, when Turnpike Exit 8A opened and the Rossmoor age-restricted community was developed. Many more followed, and the census designated places include Rossmoor (2,992 people in 2020), Clearbrook (2,909), Concordia (2,455), Whittingham (2,348), Monroe Manor (2,178), Forsgate (2,056), Regency at Monroe (2,036), Stonebridge (1,616), The Ponds (941), Renaissance (637) and Encore (625). Neighborhoods outside those are informal names such as Mill Lake Manor, Outcalt and Manor Heights.

If your house sits inside one of these communities, ask the association for its resale paperwork and any rules on who may buy, since the township's own forms say nothing about community rules.

sections.h2: Does a Monroe sale need a certificate of continued occupancy?
sections.html:
Ask the Construction Department. Chapter 39 of the township code lists a certificate of continued occupancy among its construction fees and carries the note "R-5 are optional," and R-5 is the use group for one and two family houses. The township's online forms page sends construction applications to the state Department of Community Affairs site.

Other forms a seller may touch are listed on the township forms page:

  • A residential zoning permit, listed at a $25 fee, with commercial at $100.
  • A Tenancy Review Application and a Landlord Identity Registration for rented houses.
  • A Foreclosed Property Registration Form for vacant bank-owned homes.
  • Septic Site Evaluation and Well Application forms through the Health Department.

The fee chapter also notes that garden-type sheds of 200 square feet or less and 10 feet or less in height do not need a permit, and that roofing or siding on a detached one or two family house does not need one unless the siding is polypropylene. Ask the Construction Department for the permit history on the address before you list.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and hospitals compare for Monroe buyers?
sections.html:
Buyers here trade commute time for space and age-restricted housing.

  • Roads: Turnpike Exit 8A, with a nine-lane toll gate, sits at the township's western edge. Route 32, Route 33 and a long list of county routes cross the township, which has about 176 miles of roadway.
  • Bus: NJ Transit routes 138 and 139 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and Coach USA Suburban Transit and Academy Bus provide weekday commuter service to the terminal and Wall Street.
  • Rail: the nearest stations are Metuchen, New Brunswick and Princeton Junction on the Northeast Corridor.
  • Local shuttle: a Middlesex County Area Transit line links Jamesburg and the New Brunswick station.

CentraState Healthcare System's 287-bed hospital in Freehold Township is the nearest, and Penn Medicine Princeton Medical Center, Raritan Bay Medical Center and two New Brunswick hospitals are close.

sections.h2: How do Monroe schools and parks look to a buyer?
sections.html:
The Monroe Township School District has eight schools and 6,906 students in 2023-24, with 12.6 students per classroom teacher. Applegarth, Barclay Brook, Brookside, Mill Lake, Oak Tree and Woodland are the elementary schools, Monroe Township Middle School has 1,704 students and Monroe Township High School has 2,620. About 300 students from Jamesburg also attend the high school. Eighth graders across Middlesex County may apply to the county magnet schools, which charge no tuition.

Thompson Park is a 675-acre county park on the Monroe and Jamesburg line and the largest in the Middlesex County Park System, with Lake Manalapan, trails, a dog park and a small zoo. Monroe has three cricket fields, and its high school started New Jersey's first high school cricket team in 2023.

sections.h2: How are Monroe property taxes split, and when are they due?
sections.html:
Monroe tax bills are paid quarterly and are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. The township's own facts page reported a 2022 general tax rate of 2.517 per $100 of assessed value, made up of county 0.461, school 1.470, municipal 0.489, county open space 0.039, municipal open space 0.015 and library 0.043. A fire district adds 0.135, 0.150 or 0.224 depending on whether the house is in District 1, 2 or 3, so check your bill for the district. The township says only 20 cents of each tax dollar goes to municipal operations and local open space, with school, county and fire district budgets making up roughly 80 percent.

The Assessor's forms page carries the senior and disability deduction, veteran's deduction, farmland assessment and the petition of appeal. For ANCHOR benefits, the township points residents to the State Department of Treasury hotline at 1-888-238-1233.

sections.h2: What is the Middlesex County appeal deadline, and what does the seller owe the state?
sections.html:
Middlesex County is not on the alternative calendar, so the Division of Taxation's general rule applies: petitions must be received by April 1, or May 1 where a municipal revaluation has taken place. The county Board of Taxation has voted not to hold virtual hearings. Assessments above $1,000,000 can go directly to the State Tax Court.

sections.h2: Where is a Monroe deed recorded?
sections.html: The Middlesex County Clerk records deeds at 75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick, from 8:30 am to 4:10 pm on weekdays, and you must arrive by 4 pm. Appointments are not required but are served first. A paper deed needs original signatures with printed names, the words "Prepared by," the tax block, lot and consideration, and a record and return address. A paper cover sheet is required, and leaving it off adds a $20 indexing charge. E-recordings are an alternative and skip the cover sheet.

faqs.q: Which Monroe Township does this page cover?
faqs.a: It covers Monroe Township in Middlesex County, ZIP 08831, with its municipal building on Municipal Plaza. Monroe Township in Gloucester County is a separate town near Williamstown with different rules.

faqs.q: Does Monroe Township in Middlesex County require a resale certificate?
faqs.a: Ask the Construction Department. The township fee chapter lists a certificate of continued occupancy and marks R-5 one and two family houses as optional, so a sale may not need one.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Monroe assessment in Middlesex County?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 in a year the municipality was revalued. Gloucester, Monmouth and Burlington counties use January 15, but Middlesex follows the general state rule.

faqs.q: When are Monroe Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1 at the Tax Collector's office. The township's fire district adds a separate rate depending on whether the home is in District 1, 2 or 3.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Monroe sale?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Clerk in New Brunswick records it. Bring original signatures, a "Prepared by" line, block, lot and consideration, plus a paper cover sheet to avoid the $20 indexing charge.
